messages:
Priya S: FYI customer 'Acme' on Private (on-prem) is getting intermittent 502/connection errors when fetching models. They're in a locked-down environment behind a corporate forward proxy and cannot reach the hosted endpoints directly. Need help debugging outbound egress.

acme_ops: Logs: curl to https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health returns HTTP/1.1 407 Proxy Authentication Required. When we try openssl s_client we get an HTML auth page instead of a cert, and sometimes 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'.

Jamie N: Two likely causes: (1) proxy requiring auth/CONNECT (407) or (2) proxy doing TLS interception (MITM) and replacing certs (x509 errors). Can you paste output of: `env | egrep -i proxy`, `curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health`, and `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -showcerts`? Also capture tcpdump of the handshake if possible.

acme_ops: env shows HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:8080 and NO_PROXY is empty. curl -v prints 407 then an HTML login page. We can't disable the proxy for non-admin reasons.

Jamie N: OK. Short checklist for on-prem/private:
1) Ensure proxy allows CONNECT to api.redwood-inference.com:443 and any S3/model store endpoints used for model pulls.
2) If the proxy performs TLS MITM, either: install the corporate CA into the Private runtime trust store OR configure the proxy to passthrough (no MITM) for redwood hosts.
3) Ensure DNS resolves the public hostnames inside the environment; host-based allowlists are preferred over IPs.

Priya S: Customer needs exact commands to collect diagnostics and a minimal repro.

Jamie N: Repro/debug commands to run: 
```
# check proxy env
env | egrep -i 'proxy'
# verbose curl via proxy
curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
# direct openssl test (shows cert chain)
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com < /dev/null
# tcpdump capture for TLS handshake
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host api.redwood-inference.com and port 443 -w /tmp/redwood_tls.pcap
```
If curl returns HTML before TLS, the proxy is intercepting. If openssl returns the real cert chain when you bypass proxy (or when NO_PROXY is set) that proves MITM/auth behavior.

acme_ops: We ran the commands. When we set `NO_PROXY=api.redwood-inference.com` curl returns HTTP 200 and /v1/health is OK. With NO_PROXY unset, we again get the proxy login HTML. So NO_PROXY bypass fixes the API health check. Model downloads still fail with 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority' towards S3 endpoints.

Jamie N: That confirms the proxy intercepts TLS. Options: 
- If feasible, add the redwood hostnames (api.redwood-inference.com, model-store.redwood.s3.amazonaws.com, and any regional S3 endpoints) to NO_PROXY for the Redwood runtime/service.
- If MITM can't be disabled, install the corporate CA into the runtime's trust store. Examples: place PEM in /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/company.crt and run `update-ca-certificates` on Debian-based images, or update JVM cacerts for Java-based runtimes.
- Alternatively configure the proxy to allow CONNECT passthrough for those hosts.

Priya S: Also confirm firewall rules. Customers sometimes whitelist IP ranges instead of hostnames, which is brittle because upstream S3 IPs change. Prefer host-based allowlists and proxy CONNECT allow rules. Example firewall snippet (host IP-based):
```
# allow outbound HTTPS to a CIDR used by model fetch (example only)
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 54.210.123.0/24 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
```
But recommend host whitelisting on the proxy layer.

eng-infra: @Priya opened ticket INF-4827 with our infra team. Please attach tcpdump, curl -v, and openssl outputs. If customer cannot change proxy config, we can propose a sidecar proxy/fwd that sits in a DMZ egress node that has passthrough.

acme_ops: We'll try installing the corporate root CA into the image and test model download. If that fails, we'll request a bypass for s3.amazonaws.com.

infra-bot: Incident created: INF-4827 | Priority P2 | assigned: eng-infra

Mike Support: Marking as escalated. I'll coordinate a screenshare with customer and eng if they need help applying the CA or changing NO_PROXY. :thumbsup:

acme_ops: Update: Installing the corp CA allowed model download for some regions, but a regional S3 endpoint still failed — appears to be SNI-based routing at the proxy. Requesting proxy team to passthrough for *.s3.amazonaws.com.

Jamie N: If proxy enforces SNI inspection, it must either present a trusted cert (install CA) or bypass for those hostnames. We'll include the list of FQDNs used by our model puller in the ticket.

Priya S: Provisional close here pending customer confirmation and proxy-side changes. If they can't change proxy rules, we'll help them deploy a lightweight egress forwarder that originates connections from an approved egress zone.
